question: What is the main advantage of .claude/rules/ over CLAUDE.md?

options.text: Rules have higher priority
options.explanation: Priority is not an advantage of rules. All instructions are merged and applied together

options.text: Rules support Markdown, while CLAUDE.md does not
options.explanation: Both formats use Markdown. The difference is not in format, but in the loading mechanism

options.text: Rules support more lines of text
options.explanation: There are no file size limits for either CLAUDE.md or rules. The difference is in modularity and lazy loading

options.text: Rules with path-specific frontmatter load only when working with matching files, saving context
options.explanation: Correct! Lazy loading is the key advantage. TypeScript rules don't consume context when the agent works with CSS or Dockerfiles

question:
What does this frontmatter in a rule file mean?

---
paths:
  - "src/**/*.{ts,tsx}"
---

options.text: The rule applies to all project files
options.explanation: The pattern is specific: only .ts and .tsx files in src/. For all files, the pattern would be **/*

options.text: The rule prohibits editing these files
options.explanation: paths defines when the rule loads into context, not file access restrictions

options.text: The rule loads only when working with .ts and .tsx files in the src/ directory
options.explanation: Correct! The glob pattern src/**/*.{ts,tsx} matches TypeScript files in src/ and all subdirectories. The rule loads only when working with these files

options.text: The rule creates new files at the specified path
options.explanation: paths is a loading filter, not a file creation instruction

question: What is the recommended context window distribution?

options.text: 50% instructions, 25% history, 25% working space
options.explanation: 50% for instructions is too much. The agent won't have enough space to read files and perform tasks

options.text: 25% instructions, 25% history, 50% working space
options.explanation: Correct! Half the context should be free for working space -- reading files, command results, diff contents

options.text: 33% for each category equally
options.explanation: Working space needs more room than instructions or history, because project files are usually the most voluminous

options.text: Distribution doesn't matter, context is unlimited
options.explanation: The context window is always limited. Proper distribution is key to efficient agent work

question: What happens if a file in .claude/rules/ has no frontmatter with paths?

options.text: The file loads only on explicit user request
options.explanation: Files in rules/ load automatically. Without frontmatter -- always, with frontmatter -- on paths match

options.text: The file will load on every launch, as if it were part of CLAUDE.md
options.explanation: Correct! Without frontmatter, the rule is considered always-on and loads in every session. This works for global rules (security), but loses the lazy loading advantage

options.text: Claude Code will throw an error
options.explanation: Frontmatter is optional. Without it, the file just loads always

options.text: The file will be ignored
options.explanation: On the contrary -- a file without frontmatter loads always, not ignored

options.text: Context is 50-70% full
options.explanation: Good time for /compact -- not critical yet, but time to free up space

options.text: Before a large task requiring many files
options.explanation: If reading many files is ahead, it's worth freeing context from unnecessary history

options.text: Preventively at the start of every session
options.explanation: At session start the context is clean -- /compact has nothing to compress

options.text: Long conversation with many steps
options.explanation: Long history takes a significant portion of context. /compact summarizes it, preserving key decisions

options.text: /compact works faster, /clear is slower
options.explanation: Speed is not the key difference. The difference is whether conversation context is preserved

options.text: /compact deletes project files, /clear does not
options.explanation: Neither /compact nor /clear touch project files. Both commands work only with session context

options.text: They do the same thing
options.explanation: /compact preserves context in compressed form, /clear removes it entirely. This is a significant difference

options.text: /compact compresses history, preserving key points; /clear completely resets the session
options.explanation: Correct! /compact is 'smart compression': summarizes the conversation but remembers key decisions. /clear is a full reset, as if you just launched Claude Code

question: What are sub-agents in the context of context window management?

options.text: Copies of CLAUDE.md for different directories
options.explanation: Subdirectory CLAUDE.md is a separate concept. Sub-agents are parallel agent sessions

options.text: Plugins for Claude Code
options.explanation: Plugins are a separate extension mechanism. Sub-agents are a way to decompose tasks for context saving

options.text: Other developers on the team
options.explanation: Sub-agents are not people, but separate Claude Code processes with their own context

options.text: Separate agent sessions with their own context for isolated sub-tasks
options.explanation: Correct! A sub-agent performs a task in its own context and returns only the result, not loading the main context with intermediate step details

question: Which glob pattern is suitable for rules that should apply ONLY to React components?

options.text: src/components/**/*.tsx
options.explanation: Correct! This pattern precisely targets .tsx files in the components directory. You can add src/pages/**/*.tsx for pages
This pattern matches all TypeScript files, not just React components. It would include utilities, API routes, configs

options.text: *.tsx
options.explanation: Without ** this pattern matches only .tsx files in the project root, not in subdirectories
This pattern matches any file -- too broad. The rule will load always

question: You have a monorepo with a React frontend and Express backend. What is the optimal rule organization strategy?

options.text: Everything in CLAUDE.md -- React rules, Express rules, tests
options.explanation: When working on frontend, backend rules waste context, and vice versa

options.text: General in CLAUDE.md, React rules and Express rules -- in separate rules/ files with paths
options.explanation: Correct! CLAUDE.md for build commands and general architecture. rules/react.md with paths for packages/web/**, rules/api.md with paths for packages/api/**. Each rule set loads only when working with its part of the project

options.text: Separate CLAUDE.md in each package directory
options.explanation: Subdirectory CLAUDE.md is also an option, but rules/ with paths give more flexible control and better organization

options.text: Don't use any instructions, the agent will figure it out
options.explanation: Without instructions, the agent will guess project conventions, waste context on exploration, and make inconsistent decisions

question: Which of these rules should be made always-on (without paths)?

options.text: React components must be functional
options.explanation: This rule is relevant only when working with React components (.tsx), better with paths

options.text: SQL queries through ORM, not raw SQL
options.explanation: This rule is relevant only when working with database files, better tied to paths

options.text: All secrets through environment variables
options.explanation: This is a universal security rule, relevant for any file

options.text: Never hardcode API keys
options.explanation: Security rules are needed when working with any file -- they should be always-on

question: Context is 85% full, you need to start a new unrelated task. What's the best action?

options.text: Keep working, context will free up automatically
options.explanation: Context does not free up automatically. At 85% full, agent quality is already degrading

options.text: Delete some rules from rules/
options.explanation: Deleting rules is a destructive action that affects all future sessions. To free context, use /clear

options.text: Use /compact to compress history
options.explanation: /compact would help, but at 85% and switching to an unrelated task, a full reset is better. /compact would keep the old task's context, which is useless for the new task

options.text: Use /clear for a full session reset
options.explanation: Correct! When switching to an unrelated task, /clear is the best choice. You'll start with clean context, CLAUDE.md and rules/ will reload automatically

question: Why is it bad to have dozens of small files in rules/ (one rule in each)?

options.text: Each file has overhead (frontmatter, headings), many small files create unnecessary load
options.explanation: Correct! Frontmatter + heading in each file -- these are tokens. 20 files with one rule each will spend more context than 3-4 thematic files with the same rules

options.text: Small files load slower
options.explanation: Loading speed is not the problem. The problem is context window consumption on overhead

options.text: Git can't handle many files
options.explanation: Git handles any number of files fine. The problem is not git, but context usage efficiency

options.text: Claude Code doesn't support more than 10 files in rules/
options.explanation: There's no technical limit on file count. The problem is organization and overhead

question: What is the claudeMdExcludes setting for?

options.text: For hiding CLAUDE.md from git
options.explanation: .gitignore is used to hide from git. claudeMdExcludes is a Claude Code setting

options.text: For excluding certain CLAUDE.md and rules from loading by glob patterns
options.explanation: Correct! claudeMdExcludes lets you specify which CLAUDE.md or rules should not be loaded. Useful in monorepos where another team's CLAUDE.md is not needed

options.text: For deleting CLAUDE.md files from the project
options.explanation: claudeMdExcludes does not delete files, it excludes them from loading into context

options.text: For restricting access of other users
options.explanation: claudeMdExcludes is not related to access rights. It's an instruction loading filter

question: You noticed instructions take ~40% of the context window. What to do?

options.text: Delete CLAUDE.md entirely
options.explanation: Deleting CLAUDE.md deprives the agent of critically important instructions: build commands, architecture, constraints. You need to optimize, not delete

options.text: Use claudeMdExcludes for unneeded rules
options.explanation: If some rules or CLAUDE.md from other parts of the monorepo are not needed -- exclude them

options.text: Shorten formulations, remove extra examples
options.explanation: More concise formulations = fewer tokens. No need to describe each rule with three examples

options.text: Remove duplication between CLAUDE.md and rules/
options.explanation: If a rule is described in both places -- it loads twice. Remove duplication

options.text: Add paths to rules/ files that don't have frontmatter
options.explanation: Files without paths load always. Adding paths makes them lazy-loaded and frees context
